title: Expired shares continue to authorize document reads

trace.description: GET /documents/{doc_id} authenticates and resolves requested document
can_read policy; original version omits required predicate

evidence.description: test_expired_share_denied and test_expiry_exact_boundary_denied fail with 200 != 404 before fix
All 12 regression/control tests pass after fix

counterevidence: Share creation rejects past expiration (original app.py:60), and reads reject revoked shares (original :43). Neither evaluates elapsed time on a later read. Owner access is intentionally independent of shares.

likelihood.reason: Requires a previously legitimate grant or ownership and subsequent expiry/migration.

impact.reason: Fully defeats the explicit access withdrawal or tenant boundary and discloses full document contents.

conditions.description: A same-tenant recipient has a legitimate share whose expiration has elapsed.

ext.description: An authenticated recipient requests a previously shared document after the grant expires and receives its full JSON. The original read policy checked document, recipient and revoked only; it never checked expires_at. At the exact expiry boundary it also returned 200 instead of 404.

title: Document reads ignore current tenant membership

trace.description: GET /documents/{doc_id} authenticates and resolves requested document
can_read policy; original version omits required predicate

evidence.description: All 12 regression/control tests pass after fix

counterevidence: actor resolves current user state, and share/revoke require owner plus current tenant (original app.py:58 and :74). Those controls do not execute in the read path. Revocation and document/recipient matching limit access to formerly authorized resources but do not enforce membership.

likelihood.reason: Requires a previously legitimate grant or ownership and subsequent expiry/migration.

impact.reason: Fully defeats the explicit access withdrawal or tenant boundary and discloses full document contents.

conditions.description: A trusted directory has moved the authenticated owner or live-share recipient to another tenant; the document remains in its original tenant.

ext.description: A previously authorized owner or share recipient can GET a document from the original tenant after a trusted directory migration to another tenant. The original can_read ignored its user argument, so both branches bypassed the required current-tenant boundary and returned full document JSON.
